Where we left off

Session 01 gave you an idea.
Tonight we find out if it's real.

Idea Forge got each of you to a sharpened concept. That concept is a set of guesses — about who hurts, how much, and who'd pay to make it stop. Discovery is the discipline of testing those guesses before you spend a year and a payroll proving them wrong.

A startup is a temporary organization built to search for a repeatable, profitable, scalable business model.

Everything is committed before the first customer says a word. The first real data point arrives at Launch — the most expensive possible place to learn you were wrong.

Source: The Four Steps to the Epiphany, Steve Blank
A war story

My $7.1M ServerVault Lesson

Outside: built to a fortress spec.
Inside: every component, capital committed before validated demand.

Steel, cooling, security, racks — flawless. The question nobody falsified: at this price, who actually needs the fortress? The most expensive thing you can build is the wrong thing — built perfectly.

The lens — everything tonight answers these

The Four Foundation Questions

01 What problem do you solve?
02 Who’s got it?
03 What’s the impact of the problem?
04 What will they pay to make it go away?
Q4 is the magnitude. Who pays — often not the user — is the ecosystem’s job, next.

Stage 01

Hypotheses

Guess on purpose — in writing.

Hypotheses · the system around the user

Map the Whole Ecosystem

Zendayfus — first ecosystem pass. User here; payer over there. Drawn by hand — yours should be too.
Users — who lives with it Connected parties Payers — who opens the wallet Gatekeepers — approve / veto Data flow Money flow Secondary processes

The payer is rarely the user. Find the wallet and the gatekeeper before you fall in love with the user.

Hypotheses · the fit you're betting on

Product–Market Fit

Fit is when your square answers their circle. Strong opinions, loosely held — you'll redraw this after the interviews.

Value Proposition Canvas, after Osterwalder · your 11×17 takeaway
Hypotheses · the deliverable

Create Tests That Make You Smarter

We believe [segment] struggles with [problem] when [context].
We'll know we're right when [observable signal] — and we'll act on it at 85% conviction.
“Do you like the website?”→“What’s the one thing on the dashboard you’d use every day?” “Would you pay for this?”→“Would you pay $29.99/mo? No? How about $9.99?” “Is this a problem for you?”→“What did it cost you last quarter — in hours or dollars?” “Would you use this feature?”→“Walk me through the last time you needed it. What did you do?” “Do you think it’s a good idea?”→“Can I put you down for the September pilot?”

Stage 02

Investigate

Get out of the building.

Investigate · who first

Talk to the Left Edge

Right now you want techies and visionaries — the people who feel the problem so badly they'll tolerate a rough answer. The mainstream buys proof you don't have yet.

The full chasm story is the go-to-market session. Tonight it's just a targeting map.

Investigate · the work

25–50

Conversations

Not three. You're hunting for signal, not applause — and every one of these meetings has to be earned. AI accelerates the prep and the breadth; it cannot have the conversation for you.

Your interview pipeline — real humans, one at a time.
Investigate · IDEO method

Observe Behavior.
Don’t Just Listen

People can't always articulate their real needs — but their day reveals them. Catalog the routine and the unanticipated friction shows up where words don't.

IDEO Method Cards · A Day in the Life

Investigate · interview craft

Interview Like a Pro — The Mom Test

  • “Why?” — five times
  • “Tell me more…”
  • “Walk me through the last time that happened.”
  • “How would you describe it to someone else?”
  • “Draw me a picture.”

Anchor in real past behavior — people are unreliable narrators of their own future.

Don't sell.

A pro at work: open questions, follow the thread, never pitch. (CBS News / 60 Minutes)
Rob Fitzpatrick · The Mom Test (on your reading list)
Investigate · IDEO method

What You Assume ≠
What They Live

The deadly gap is between the founder's picture of the customer and the customer's actual experience. Enact theirs — out loud — and watch your assumptions fall out.

IDEO Method Cards · Be Your Customer

Stage 03 · Synthesize

Turn Conversations Into Conviction

Log same-day · Cluster the pain · Score every hypothesis · Evidence over compliments

Dead End
No Verdict — Yet
Build It
0% 15% 85% 100%
0–15% · Stop

Stop right now. This is a dead end — there’s no value to be had here.

16–84% · Non-conclusive

Rearchitect your questions and go again. Still here? The market has no strong opinion — backburner it and review later.

85–100% · Build It

Run, don’t walk. You’ve found truth — and the market confirms it.

Anecdotes are noise. Convergence is signal.

Stage 04 · Red Cell

Try to Kill It

  • Why won't this work?
  • Why won't people change their behavior?
  • Why won't the gatekeeper say yes?
  • Is the price actually justifiable?

We attack the idea so the founder doesn't waste a year. The idea — never the person.
